Stereodivergent Palladium- and Rhodium-Catalyzed Intramolecular
Addition of Tosylureas to Allenes: Diastereoselective Synthesis of
Tetrahydropyrimidinones
Arne G. A. Geissler, Jasmin R. Riesterer, and Bernhard Breit *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 9168 −9172 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: The intramolecular addition of tosylureas to allenes is highly syn-/anti-diastereoselective when employing a palladium
or rhodium-based catalytic system and a ﬀords 1,3-cyclic ureas. Under palladium catalysis a range of thermodynamic anti-
tetrahydropyrimidinones are accessible, while rhodium catalysis allows synthesis of the kinetic syn-tetrahydropyrimidinones. For a
representative scope of substrates both cyclic ureas were obtained in excellent yields and diastereoselectivities. The obtained
tetrahydropyrimidinones were shown to be easily deprotected and modi ﬁed to demonstrate the synthetic value.
T
etrahydropyrimidinones and the related 1,3-diamines are
a common motif in organic chemistry and frequently
observed in natural products, 1 drugs,2 and ligands.3 In contrast
to traditional synthetic approaches, 4 more e ﬃcient and direct
catalytic methods for the synthesis of tetrahydropyrimidinones,
which can be conveniently transformed into a 1,3-diamine,
were recently discovered. Menche reported a Pd-catalyzed
intramolecular allylic substitution of allylcarbonates, resulting
in 1,3-disubstituted tetrahydropyrimidinones.
5 Variation of the
solvent allowed stereodivergent synthesis of syn- and anti-
tetrahydropyrimidinones in excellent yields and diastereose-
lectivities. A powerful isomerization/amination method was
published by White, who applied Pd-catalyzed C −H-oxidation
in allylic position to access 1,2-imidazolidinones.
6 This concept
was extended to carbamides by Hara. 7 The use of White ’s
Pd(TFA)2/bis-sulfoxide catalyst and stoichiometric oxidant led
to 1,2-imidazolidinones and 1,3-tetrahydropyrimidinones.
In the past decade, methods for the catalytic addition of
pronucleophiles to alkynes and allenes have been developed as
an atom economic
8 alternative to the allylic substitution. 9
Earlier studies in this ﬁeld showed that the addition of N-
pronucleophiles to allenes by late transition metal catalysis
leads to valuable branched allylic products in excellent yields
and selectivities.
10,11 Very recently we reported the intra-
molecular enantioselective addition of tosylamides to terminal
and internal allenes.
12 Yet the necessity of chiral ligands and
matched/mismatched situations still prove to be challenging.
This problem was addressed in previous work by our group. By
taking advantage of the relative con ﬁguration in the product,
diﬀerent catalytic systems were developed for the intra-
molecular diastereoselective addition of amides 13 and
carbamates14 to allenes. These methods encouraged us to
investigate the herein reported intramolecular addition of
tosylureas to allenes.
Cyclization of 1a in the presence of a palladium catalyst and
phenylisobutyric acid gave an 85% combined yield of a 1:1
mixture of both diastereomers 2a and 3a (Table 1, entry 1). A
change of additive toward a decreased amount of benzoic acid
improved the yield to 99% and diastereoselectivity to 20:1 in
favor of 2a (entry 2).
15 With a suitable method for the
preparation of the anti-diastereomer in hand, we conducted a
broad screening of di ﬀerent conditions, additives, and catalytic
systems in favor of syn-selectivity.15 A major amount of 3a was
observed exclusively under rhodium catalysis. Using PPTS/

LiCl as additive, which worked ﬁne in the cyclization of
carbamates, gave a poor yield and selectivity (entry 3). For
benzoic acid an increase of syn-selectivity was observed, as well
as an increase in yield to 83%. In an extensive screening
pentaﬂuorobenzoic acid was found to give an excellent yield
and a good diastereoselectivity of 5:1 (entry 5).
A decrease in temperature to 50 °C led to an increase in
diastereoselectivity, yet incomplete conversion (entry 6).
Increasing the catalyst load at 50 °C pushed the yield to
95%, while maintaining a high diastereoselectivity of 10:1 in
favor of 3a (entry 7).
With suitable methods for both diastereomers in hand, a
scope of substrates were tested in syn- and anti-diastereose-
lective cyclization. Under palladium-catalysis conditions we
achieved an average yield of 86% and average d.r. of 18:1
(Scheme 1).
16 We were able to show that di ﬀerent halogenated
aryl groups were tolerated. The ortho-brominated substrate 1b
gave a slightly lower yield of 2b, probably due to side-reactions.
2e and 2f were synthesized in excellent yield and selectivity.
Electron-rich functions in 1g, 1h, and 1i were well tolerated
just as the electron-withdrawing functionality in 1j. Further-
more, steric demands in the naphthyl-derivative 1k were found
to be unproblematic, giving 2k in 86% yield. Cyclization of
aliphatic 1l and 1m worked in good yields with a slight drop in
d.r. to 10:1 for 2l. The nitro-containing 2n was obtained with a
d.r. slightly below the average. Performing catalysis on the
heteroaromatic furyl-substrate 1o gave a pleasing 81% yield of
2o.
Rhodium catalysis allowed access to the valuable syn-
tetrahydropyrimidinones 3a−o in an average yield of 76% and
average d.r. of 7:1 ( Scheme 2 ).
16 For the halogenated aryl-
derivatives 1b−f good yields of 68 −81% and a d.r. of 6:1 to
10:1 were achieved. In contrast, the electron-rich 2g−i were
obtained in slightly higher yield and slightly lower diaster-
eoselectivity. The electron-withdrawing nitro- and cyano-
groups in 1j and 1n led to only a moderate yield of 3j and
3n. Especially 3n was obtained with a major contamination of
the anti-isomer 2n. The aliphatic 3l and 3m were synthesized
in good yields and moderate diastereoselectivity. 1o gave a
79% yield of 3o, yet with a moderate diastereoselectivity of 3:1.
A set of exemplary follow-up reactions have been performed
on 3a (Scheme 3 ). Reductive cleavage of the tosyl group gave
4 in quantitative yield, and consequent treatment with aqueous
HCl allows access to the valuable 1,3-diamine 5-hydro-
chloride.

6 in 86% yield. Ozonolysis and reductive workup with
triphenylphosphine allow selective conversion of the ole ﬁn
group into aldehyde 7. Employing a self-assembly Rh/6-
DPPon-based catalyst system 17 allowed hydroformylation of
the ole ﬁn function in excellent linear to branched selectivity
and 76% isolated yield of 8. The free urea N −H bond can be
directly addressed in functionalization experiments as was
demonstrated in the synthesis of alkylated 9.
When isolated 2a was subjected to Rh-catalysis conditions,
no change in diastereomeric ratio was observed. However, after
subjecting 3a to palladium-catalysis conditions, almost
quantitative corrosion of the allylic stereocenter in favor of
the anti-isomer 2a was observed after 16 h.
This observation is in accordance with conducted DFT-
calculations (BP86/dev2svp), predicting 2a to be 2.4 kcal
more stable than 3a, therefore 2a being the thermodynamic
and 3a being the kinetic product of the described cyclization
(Scheme 4 ).
In accordance to the proposed mechanisms for the rhodium
catalyzed addition of pronucleophiles to allenes and
alkynes,
13,18 in particular the catalyzed cyclization of allenyl
sulfonylcarbamates,14 a mechanism for the rhodium catalyzed
diastereoselective cyclization of tosylureas has been devised
(Scheme 5 ). For syn-selective conditions, electron-de ﬁcient
carboxylic acids were shown to increase yield and selectivity
and may help to generate the active rhodium-hydride
intermediate A by formation of a suitable precatalyst as was

recently described by Heller and Breit. 18b Hydrometalation of
the allene results in the cyclic π-allyl complex B which
undergoes reductive elimination throughout an inner-sphere
reductive elimination to yield the kinetic syn-product 3a. This
step seems to be irreversible under the described syn-
conditions and is favored for strong carboxylic acids, posing
weakly coordinating counterions.
Under anti-selective conditions, palladium is able to reinsert
into the allylic C −N bond and generate the open π-allyl
complex C in which the catalytic center is saturated with
carboxylate. Complex C is also intermediate after hydro-
palladation of allene 1a. Due to the carboxylate blocking the
coordination of the urea functionality, an outer-sphere attack is
proposed that favors the formation of the thermodynamically
more stable anti-product 2a.
Summarizing we demonstrated the intramolecular addition
of tosylureas to allenes to be an e ﬃcient method for the
diastereoselective preparation of tetrahydropyrimidinones,
which are a valuable precursor for the 1,3-diamine motif.
Through careful choice of catalyst, both the kinetic syn-
tetrahydropyrimidinones and thermodynamic anti- tetrahydro-
pyrimidinones are accessible in high yields and selectivities.
Diﬀerent follow-up reactions were demonstrated, such as
cleavage into the diamine, aldehyde formation, and alkylation.
In the future, we are looking to apply our new method in
diﬀerent applications and natural product syntheses.

Stereodivergent Palladium- and Rhodium-Catalyzed Intramolecular
Addition of Tosylureas to Allenes: Diastereoselective Synthesis of
Tetrahydropyrimidinones
Arne G. A. Geissler, Jasmin R. Riesterer, and Bernhard Breit *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 9168 −9172 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: The intramolecular addition of tosylureas to allenes is highly syn-/anti-diastereoselective when employing a palladium
or rhodium-based catalytic system and a ﬀords 1,3-cyclic ureas. Under palladium catalysis a range of thermodynamic anti-
tetrahydropyrimidinones are accessible, while rhodium catalysis allows synthesis of the kinetic syn-tetrahydropyrimidinones. For a
representative scope of substrates both cyclic ureas were obtained in excellent yields and diastereoselectivities. The obtained
tetrahydropyrimidinones were shown to be easily deprotected and modi ﬁed to demonstrate the synthetic value.
T
etrahydropyrimidinones and the related 1,3-diamines are
a common motif in organic chemistry and frequently
observed in natural products, 1 drugs,2 and ligands.3 In contrast
to traditional synthetic approaches, 4 more e ﬃcient and direct
catalytic methods for the synthesis of tetrahydropyrimidinones,
which can be conveniently transformed into a 1,3-diamine,
were recently discovered. Menche reported a Pd-catalyzed
intramolecular allylic substitution of allylcarbonates, resulting
in 1,3-disubstituted tetrahydropyrimidinones.
5 Variation of the
solvent allowed stereodivergent synthesis of syn- and anti-
tetrahydropyrimidinones in excellent yields and diastereose-
lectivities. A powerful isomerization/amination method was
published by White, who applied Pd-catalyzed C −H-oxidation
in allylic position to access 1,2-imidazolidinones.
6 This concept
was extended to carbamides by Hara. 7 The use of White ’s
Pd(TFA)2/bis-sulfoxide catalyst and stoichiometric oxidant led
to 1,2-imidazolidinones and 1,3-tetrahydropyrimidinones.
In the past decade, methods for the catalytic addition of
pronucleophiles to alkynes and allenes have been developed as
an atom economic
8 alternative to the allylic substitution. 9
Earlier studies in this ﬁeld showed that the addition of N-
pronucleophiles to allenes by late transition metal catalysis
leads to valuable branched allylic products in excellent yields
and selectivities.
10,11 Very recently we reported the intra-
molecular enantioselective addition of tosylamides to terminal
and internal allenes.
12 Yet the necessity of chiral ligands and
matched/mismatched situations still prove to be challenging.
This problem was addressed in previous work by our group. By
taking advantage of the relative con ﬁguration in the product,
diﬀerent catalytic systems were developed for the intra-
molecular diastereoselective addition of amides 13 and
carbamates14 to allenes. These methods encouraged us to
investigate the herein reported intramolecular addition of
tosylureas to allenes.
Cyclization of 1a in the presence of a palladium catalyst and
phenylisobutyric acid gave an 85% combined yield of a 1:1
mixture of both diastereomers 2a and 3a (Table 1, entry 1). A
change of additive toward a decreased amount of benzoic acid
improved the yield to 99% and diastereoselectivity to 20:1 in
favor of 2a (entry 2).
15 With a suitable method for the
preparation of the anti-diastereomer in hand, we conducted a
broad screening of di ﬀerent conditions, additives, and catalytic
systems in favor of syn-selectivity.15 A major amount of 3a was
observed exclusively under rhodium catalysis. Using PPTS/

carbamates, gave a poor yield and selectivity (entry 3). For
benzoic acid an increase of syn-selectivity was observed, as well
as an increase in yield to 83%. In an extensive screening
pentaﬂuorobenzoic acid was found to give an excellent yield
and a good diastereoselectivity of 5:1 (entry 5).
A decrease in temperature to 50 °C led to an increase in
diastereoselectivity, yet incomplete conversion (entry 6).
Increasing the catalyst load at 50 °C pushed the yield to
95%, while maintaining a high diastereoselectivity of 10:1 in
favor of 3a (entry 7).
With suitable methods for both diastereomers in hand, a
scope of substrates were tested in syn- and anti-diastereose-
lective cyclization. Under palladium-catalysis conditions we
achieved an average yield of 86% and average d.r. of 18:1
(Scheme 1).
16 We were able to show that di ﬀerent halogenated
aryl groups were tolerated. The ortho-brominated substrate 1b
gave a slightly lower yield of 2b, probably due to side-reactions.
2e and 2f were synthesized in excellent yield and selectivity.
Electron-rich functions in 1g, 1h, and 1i were well tolerated
just as the electron-withdrawing functionality in 1j. Further-
more, steric demands in the naphthyl-derivative 1k were found
to be unproblematic, giving 2k in 86% yield. Cyclization of
aliphatic 1l and 1m worked in good yields with a slight drop in
d.r. to 10:1 for 2l. The nitro-containing 2n was obtained with a
d.r. slightly below the average. Performing catalysis on the
heteroaromatic furyl-substrate 1o gave a pleasing 81% yield of
2o.
Rhodium catalysis allowed access to the valuable syn-
tetrahydropyrimidinones 3a−o in an average yield of 76% and
average d.r. of 7:1 ( Scheme 2 ).
16 For the halogenated aryl-
derivatives 1b−f good yields of 68 −81% and a d.r. of 6:1 to
10:1 were achieved. In contrast, the electron-rich 2g−i were
obtained in slightly higher yield and slightly lower diaster-
eoselectivity. The electron-withdrawing nitro- and cyano-
groups in 1j and 1n led to only a moderate yield of 3j and
3n. Especially 3n was obtained with a major contamination of
the anti-isomer 2n. The aliphatic 3l and 3m were synthesized
in good yields and moderate diastereoselectivity. 1o gave a
79% yield of 3o, yet with a moderate diastereoselectivity of 3:1.
A set of exemplary follow-up reactions have been performed
on 3a (Scheme 3 ). Reductive cleavage of the tosyl group gave
4 in quantitative yield, and consequent treatment with aqueous
HCl allows access to the valuable 1,3-diamine 5-hydro-
chloride.

triphenylphosphine allow selective conversion of the ole ﬁn
group into aldehyde 7. Employing a self-assembly Rh/6-
DPPon-based catalyst system 17 allowed hydroformylation of
the ole ﬁn function in excellent linear to branched selectivity
and 76% isolated yield of 8. The free urea N −H bond can be
directly addressed in functionalization experiments as was
demonstrated in the synthesis of alkylated 9.
When isolated 2a was subjected to Rh-catalysis conditions,
no change in diastereomeric ratio was observed. However, after
subjecting 3a to palladium-catalysis conditions, almost
quantitative corrosion of the allylic stereocenter in favor of
the anti-isomer 2a was observed after 16 h.
This observation is in accordance with conducted DFT-
calculations (BP86/dev2svp), predicting 2a to be 2.4 kcal
more stable than 3a, therefore 2a being the thermodynamic
and 3a being the kinetic product of the described cyclization
(Scheme 4 ).
In accordance to the proposed mechanisms for the rhodium
catalyzed addition of pronucleophiles to allenes and
alkynes,
13,18 in particular the catalyzed cyclization of allenyl
sulfonylcarbamates,14 a mechanism for the rhodium catalyzed
diastereoselective cyclization of tosylureas has been devised
(Scheme 5 ). For syn-selective conditions, electron-de ﬁcient
carboxylic acids were shown to increase yield and selectivity
and may help to generate the active rhodium-hydride

recently described by Heller and Breit. 18b Hydrometalation of
the allene results in the cyclic π-allyl complex B which
undergoes reductive elimination throughout an inner-sphere
reductive elimination to yield the kinetic syn-product 3a. This
step seems to be irreversible under the described syn-
conditions and is favored for strong carboxylic acids, posing
weakly coordinating counterions.
Under anti-selective conditions, palladium is able to reinsert
into the allylic C −N bond and generate the open π-allyl
complex C in which the catalytic center is saturated with
carboxylate. Complex C is also intermediate after hydro-
palladation of allene 1a. Due to the carboxylate blocking the
coordination of the urea functionality, an outer-sphere attack is
proposed that favors the formation of the thermodynamically
more stable anti-product 2a.
Summarizing we demonstrated the intramolecular addition
of tosylureas to allenes to be an e ﬃcient method for the
diastereoselective preparation of tetrahydropyrimidinones,
which are a valuable precursor for the 1,3-diamine motif.
Through careful choice of catalyst, both the kinetic syn-
tetrahydropyrimidinones and thermodynamic anti- tetrahydro-
pyrimidinones are accessible in high yields and selectivities.
Diﬀerent follow-up reactions were demonstrated, such as
cleavage into the diamine, aldehyde formation, and alkylation.
In the future, we are looking to apply our new method in
diﬀerent applications and natural product syntheses.
